column1: # Conformance vectors of the outcomes of a write for an adapter of the stores of ecd, from specs/ecd_stores/ecd_stores.contract.md
# (#outcomes, #idempotency) and the SQLite owner's mapping in ecd_stores.design.md#state-schema (Outcomes). Every adapter in every
# runtime passes every case (contract #conformance, Outcome vectors). Identity and key-order vectors are not here: they are those of
# LOOSE cases: io_commit_readback and full_open accept "rev=1 or absent" until a harness forces each landing (check sharp_landing_cases in rows.tsv).
# A case is a sequence on one fresh store; its rows run in step order. Columns are separated by one tab; "-" stands for an absent value.
#   step          the step's number in the case, from 1
#   request       create (insert, absent), update (replace at a revision), get (read); get on a poisoned handle reopens first
#   key           a symbolic name; the harness mints one Ecd ID per name before the case's first step and reuses it for every retry (idempotency 1)
#   precondition  absent (create) or rev=N (update); "-" for get
#   size          the value's length in bytes; the limit is 65536 (design state-schema: CHECK length(value) <= 65536); "-" for get
#   fault         injected before the step: - | io-at-commit (the COMMIT returns an I/O error) | full-rolled-back (SQLITE_FULL, the transaction rolled back,

#                 connection in autocommit) | space-freed (PRAGMA max_page_count raised, so the volume has room again) | full-open (SQLITE_FULL, the transaction left open; made through a test hook at commit, because SQLite rolls a single statement back on SQLITE_FULL, so max_page_count cannot leave a transaction open) | busy (the file's write lock is held elsewhere past the call's bound)
#   want_outcome  committed | conflict | refused | unknown (contract #outcomes; never "not sent" in process); "a or b" accepts either; refused:first-cause means
#                 the refusal carries the cause of the fault that poisoned the handle; for a get: found | absent
#   want_readback the key's stored state after the step, as a get on the same handle reads it: absent, rev=N, or "rev=N or absent" when the fault leaves it open;
#                 "-" when the step reads nothing back;
#   source        the contract or design line the row comes from
